lessons.title: Inspect command help
lessons.focus: Get-Help explains cmdlets, concepts, syntax, parameters, and examples without leaving the PowerShell session.
breakdown: The command name selects the help topic.
-Parameter narrows the page to one parameter.
lessons.task: Print the name of Get-ChildItem's Path parameter from local help.
hints: Select the Name property from the parameter help object.

checks.description: The Path parameter name was printed.

lessons.completion: Help is discoverable from the shell; add -Examples or -Full when you need more context.

lessons.title: Inspect another parameter
lessons.focus: Parameter help isolates the syntax and meaning of one option.
lessons.task: Print the name of Get-ChildItem's Filter parameter from local help.
hints: Start with Get-Help; use Get-Help Get-Help -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Check whether a parameter is required
lessons.focus: Help parameter objects expose metadata such as Name and Required.
lessons.task: Print Recurse:<required-value> for Copy-Item's Recurse parameter.
hints: Start with Get-Help; use Get-Help Get-Help -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Find matching parameters
lessons.focus: A wildcard parameter query can discover related switches without scanning a full help page.
lessons.example: Get-Help Get-ChildItem -Parameter '*Path*' | Sort-Object Name | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name
lessons.task: Use Get-Help to print Get-ChildItem parameter names containing Path, sorted alphabetically.
lessons.solution: Get-Help Get-ChildItem -Parameter '*Path*' | Sort-Object Name | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name
hints: Start with Get-Help; use Get-Help Get-Help -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Build a parameter requirement report
lessons.focus: Help metadata can be filtered and formatted into a concise preflight reference.
lessons.task: Print Force=False and Recurse=False on separate lines, sorted by parameter name, using Copy-Item help.
lessons.solution: Get-Help Copy-Item -Parameter * | Where-Object Name -in 'Force','Recurse' | Sort-Object Name | ForEach-Object { "$($_.Name)=$($_.Required)" }
hints: Start with Get-Help; use Get-Help Get-Help -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Discover available commands
lessons.focus: Get-Command searches cmdlets, functions, aliases, scripts, and applications available in the current session.
lessons.example_output:
CommandType Name        Version Source
----------- ----        ------- ------
Cmdlet      Get-Content 3.1.0.0 Microsoft.PowerShell.Management
breakdown: A precise name returns one command definition.
CommandType distinguishes cmdlets from aliases and applications.
lessons.task: Print only the command type of Get-ChildItem.
hints: Expand the CommandType property.

checks.description: Get-ChildItem was identified as a cmdlet.

lessons.completion: Get-Command is the quickest inventory of what PowerShell can run.

lessons.title: Identify a command source
lessons.focus: Command discovery objects identify the module that supplies a cmdlet.
lessons.task: Print only the source module of Get-ChildItem.
hints: Start with Get-Command; use Get-Help Get-Command -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Discover commands by noun
lessons.focus: -Noun searches the verb-noun naming system without requiring a wildcard string.
lessons.task: Print the names of all commands whose noun is Location, sorted alphabetically.
lessons.solution: Get-Command -Noun Location | Sort-Object Name | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name
hints: Start with Get-Command; use Get-Help Get-Command -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Inspect parameter metadata
lessons.focus: The Parameters dictionary exposes accepted names and types for automation and validation.
lessons.task: Print the type name of Get-ChildItem's Filter parameter.
hints: Start with Get-Command; use Get-Help Get-Command -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Inventory commands from one module
lessons.focus: Combining module filtering, command types, and sorting creates a reproducible capability inventory.
lessons.task: Print the names Get-Date and Get-Random from Microsoft.PowerShell.Utility, sorted alphabetically, by filtering that module command inventory.
lessons.solution: Get-Command -Module Microsoft.PowerShell.Utility -CommandType Cmdlet | Where-Object Name -in 'Get-Date','Get-Random' | Sort-Object Name | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name
hints: Start with Get-Command; use Get-Help Get-Command -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Resolve aliases
lessons.focus: Get-Alias shows which full PowerShell command an abbreviated alias resolves to, making unfamiliar commands easier to read.
lessons.example_output:
CommandType Name Version Source
----------- ---- ------- ------
Alias       ls -> Get-ChildItem
breakdown: ls is an alias in Windows PowerShell.
Definition contains the full target command.
lessons.task: Print the full command behind the dir alias.
hints: Expand the Definition property.
lessons.completion: Aliases are convenient interactively; full cmdlet names are clearer in scripts.

lessons.title: Resolve another familiar alias
lessons.focus: Alias records make terse interactive names traceable to their underlying commands.
lessons.task: Print the command behind the cat alias.
hints: Start with Get-Alias; use Get-Help Get-Alias -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Resolve several aliases together
lessons.focus: Get-Alias accepts multiple names so a reviewed group can be resolved in one call.
lessons.task: Print alias=definition records for dir and pwd, sorted by alias.
hints: Start with Get-Alias; use Get-Help Get-Alias -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Find aliases for a command
lessons.focus: -Definition reverses the lookup and finds every alias targeting a command.
lessons.task: Print all aliases for Get-Content, sorted alphabetically.
lessons.solution: Get-Alias -Definition Get-Content | Sort-Object Name | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name
hints: Start with Get-Alias; use Get-Help Get-Alias -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Build an alias audit
lessons.focus: A small allowlist can be resolved and formatted into an explicit audit that is safer to share than terse aliases.
lessons.task: Print alias=definition for cat, dir, ls, and pwd in alphabetical alias order.
hints: Start with Get-Alias; use Get-Help Get-Alias -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Show the current location
lessons.focus: Get-Location returns a PathInfo object for the current location instead of printing an unstructured path string.
breakdown: The current provider exposes a location.
The Path property contains its text representation.
lessons.task: Print only the absolute path of the disposable practice directory.
hints: Expand the Path property from Get-Location.

checks.description: The current practice path was printed.

lessons.completion: PowerShell locations can represent file-system paths and other providers.

lessons.title: Read the provider path
lessons.focus: The Path property provides a clean scalar path for logging or composition.
lessons.task: Print the current location as location=<absolute-path>.
hints: Start with Get-Location; use Get-Help Get-Location -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Inspect the location provider
lessons.focus: A PathInfo object also records which provider owns the current location.
lessons.task: Print only the provider name for the current location.
hints: Start with Get-Location; use Get-Help Get-Location -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Read a named location stack
lessons.focus: Push-Location can maintain named stacks and Get-Location -Stack inspects them without popping.
lessons.task: Push reports onto a stack named Work, then print the leaf of its saved location.
hints: Start with Get-Location; use Get-Help Get-Location -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Create a location trace
lessons.focus: Location objects can capture a before/after navigation trace without parsing prompt text.
lessons.task: Move into reports and print from=<original-leaf> to=reports.
hints: Start with Get-Location; use Get-Help Get-Location -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Change the current location
lessons.focus: Set-Location changes the active location for the current PowerShell process, affecting later relative paths.
breakdown: The relative path is resolved below the current directory.
A successful location change normally emits no output.
lessons.task: Change into the existing reports directory.
hints: Pass the directory name as the path.

checks.description: PowerShell entered the reports directory successfully.

lessons.completion: Set-Location changes only this disposable PowerShell process.

lessons.title: Move to a parent directory
lessons.focus: The .. path navigates one level upward using normal provider path semantics.
lessons.task: Start in projectsalpha, move to its parent with Set-Location, and print the new leaf name.
hints: Start with Set-Location; use Get-Help Set-Location -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Navigate to a path containing spaces
lessons.focus: Quoting keeps a path with spaces as one argument.
lessons.task: Move into the 'release notes' directory and print its leaf name.
hints: Start with Set-Location; use Get-Help Set-Location -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Use a literal wildcard path
lessons.focus: -LiteralPath prevents square brackets and wildcard characters in a real name from being interpreted.
lessons.task: Move into the literal directory archive[2025] and print its leaf name.
hints: Start with Set-Location; use Get-Help Set-Location -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Navigate a small project workflow
lessons.focus: Multiple Set-Location calls can follow a project path while relative paths remain anchored to the current step.
lessons.task: Move through projects, then alpha, then docs using relative Set-Location calls and print the final relative identity projects/alpha/docs.
lessons.solution: Set-Location projects; Set-Location alpha; Set-Location docs; $parts=(Get-Location).Path -split "[\\/]"; ($parts[-3..-1] -join "/")
hints: Start with Set-Location; use Get-Help Set-Location -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: List child items
lessons.focus: Get-ChildItem enumerates files, directories, registry keys, variables, and other provider-backed collections.
breakdown: Without a path, the current location is listed.
-Name returns compact names instead of FileInfo objects.
lessons.task: Print only the names of the two files in the practice directory.
hints: Combine the switches that select files and request names only.

checks.description: Both file names and no extras were printed.

lessons.completion: Get-ChildItem is PowerShell's general collection enumerator.

lessons.title: Filter by filename pattern
lessons.focus: -Filter lets the filesystem provider select matching names efficiently.
lessons.task: Print only .log filenames in the current directory, sorted alphabetically.
hints: Start with Get-ChildItem; use Get-Help Get-ChildItem -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Recurse through a tree
lessons.focus: -Recurse traverses descendants while -File keeps directories out of the result.
lessons.task: Print all .txt paths below docs as forward-slash relative paths, sorted.
hints: Start with Get-ChildItem; use Get-Help Get-ChildItem -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Include hidden files
lessons.focus: -Force reveals hidden items that the default listing omits.
lessons.task: Print the names visible with -Force, sorted, including hidden.txt.
hints: Start with Get-ChildItem; use Get-Help Get-ChildItem -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Summarize files by extension
lessons.focus: Recursive discovery can feed grouping and formatting to create a compact tree inventory.
lessons.task: Recursively count files under project by extension and print .json=2 then .ps1=3.
lessons.solution: Get-ChildItem project -Recurse -File | Group-Object Extension | Sort-Object Name | ForEach-Object { "$($_.Name)=$($_.Count)" }
hints: Start with Get-ChildItem; use Get-Help Get-ChildItem -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Inspect one item
lessons.focus: Get-Item retrieves the object representing one path so its metadata can flow through the object pipeline.
breakdown: The path resolves one FileInfo object.
Length measures the file in bytes.
lessons.task: Print only the byte length of note.txt.
hints: Expand the Length property.

checks.description: The six-byte file length was printed.

lessons.completion: Get-Item retrieves an object; Get-ChildItem enumerates a collection.

lessons.title: Read a file timestamp
lessons.focus: Get-Item returns filesystem metadata such as LastWriteTimeUtc.
lessons.task: Print the name of note.txt and confirm its item type is a file using name=<name> type=file.
hints: Start with Get-Item; use Get-Help Get-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Use a literal item path
lessons.focus: -LiteralPath retrieves names containing wildcard characters exactly as written.
lessons.task: Print the name of the literal file data[01].csv.
hints: Start with Get-Item; use Get-Help Get-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Compare item sizes
lessons.focus: Item metadata can be sorted and selected without reading file contents.
lessons.task: Print smallest.txt then largest.txt by sorting Get-Item results on Length.
lessons.solution: Get-Item smallest.txt,largest.txt | Sort-Object Length | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name
hints: Start with Get-Item; use Get-Help Get-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Build a file metadata record
lessons.focus: Selected item properties form a practical inventory record for validation or reporting.
lessons.task: Print name=app.conf bytes=12 extension=.conf using one Get-Item object.
hints: Start with Get-Item; use Get-Help Get-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Test whether a path exists
lessons.focus: Test-Path returns a Boolean and can distinguish leaves such as files from containers such as directories.
breakdown: The path is checked without opening it.
-PathType Leaf requires a non-container item.
lessons.task: Confirm that config.json exists and is a file.
hints: Use -PathType Leaf.
lessons.completion: Test-Path is useful for defensive scripts before reading, moving, or deleting paths.

lessons.title: Confirm a directory path
lessons.focus: -PathType Container distinguishes a directory from a leaf item.
lessons.task: Confirm that archive exists and is a directory.
hints: Start with Test-Path; use Get-Help Test-Path -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Test a missing path
lessons.focus: Negating Test-Path makes an absence assertion explicit.
lessons.task: Print True only if retired.log is absent.
hints: Start with Test-Path; use Get-Help Test-Path -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Test several required files
lessons.focus: A collection can be checked item by item and reduced to one readiness result.
lessons.task: Print ready=True only when app.conf, routes.json, and users.csv all exist as files.
hints: Start with Test-Path; use Get-Help Test-Path -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Audit present and missing inputs
lessons.focus: Testing a manifest of expected paths produces an actionable preflight report.
lessons.task: Print config.json=True and secrets.json=False in that order.
hints: Start with Test-Path; use Get-Help Test-Path -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Resolve an absolute path
lessons.focus: Resolve-Path converts an existing relative or wildcard path into resolved provider path objects.
breakdown: The input path must already exist.
The Path property contains the resolved absolute path.
lessons.task: Print only the absolute path to note.txt.
hints: Expand the Path property.

checks.description: The resolved file path was printed.

lessons.completion: Resolve-Path is valuable before logging or validating the exact path a script will use.

lessons.title: Resolve a wildcard set
lessons.focus: Resolve-Path expands wildcards and returns canonical paths for every match.
lessons.task: Resolve both .conf files and print only their leaf names, sorted.
hints: Start with Resolve-Path; use Get-Help Resolve-Path -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Produce a relative path
lessons.focus: -Relative returns a path relative to the current location instead of an absolute provider path.
lessons.task: Print the relative path to reportsdaily.txt with Resolve-Path -Relative.
hints: Start with Resolve-Path; use Get-Help Resolve-Path -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Resolve a literal wildcard name
lessons.focus: -LiteralPath avoids wildcard expansion before canonicalization.
lessons.task: Resolve the literal file report[final].txt and print its leaf name.
hints: Start with Resolve-Path; use Get-Help Resolve-Path -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Create a canonical path manifest
lessons.focus: Resolved paths can be normalized and labeled to make later file operations unambiguous.
lessons.task: Print alpha=<absolute-path> and beta=<absolute-path> for inputsalpha.txt and inputs eta.txt.
hints: Start with Resolve-Path; use Get-Help Resolve-Path -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Combine path segments
lessons.focus: Join-Path combines parent and child segments with the separator rules of the active PowerShell provider.
breakdown: The first argument is the parent path.
The second argument is the child segment.
lessons.task: Combine reports and daily.txt into one relative Windows path.
hints: Pass the parent first and child second.

checks.description: The Windows path segments were joined.

lessons.completion: Join-Path avoids hard-coding path separators in scripts.

lessons.title: Join several child segments
lessons.focus: Nesting Join-Path composes several components without manually inserting separators.
lessons.task: Join project, config, and app.json into one relative path.
hints: Start with Join-Path; use Get-Help Join-Path -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Join children to several roots
lessons.focus: Pipeline roots let Join-Path create the same child path below multiple parents.
lessons.task: Print bluesettings.json and greensettings.json by piping both roots to Join-Path.
hints: Start with Join-Path; use Get-Help Join-Path -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Resolve a joined path
lessons.focus: -Resolve confirms that a constructed path exists and returns its provider-resolved form.
lessons.task: Join data and inventory.csv with -Resolve, then print the leaf name.
hints: Start with Join-Path; use Get-Help Join-Path -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Build an output-path matrix
lessons.focus: Nested loops with Join-Path safely construct predictable paths across environments and artifact types.
lessons.task: Print devlogsapp.log and prodlogsapp.log in that order using Join-Path for every segment.
hints: Start with Join-Path; use Get-Help Join-Path -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Create a new item
lessons.focus: New-Item creates files, directories, and items exposed by other providers using an explicit item type.
lessons.example_output:
Directory: C:\work
Mode LastWriteTime Length Name
---- ------------- ------ ----
d---- ...                 reports
breakdown: -ItemType Directory requests a container.
-Path names the new directory.
lessons.task: Create a directory named reports and print its name.
hints: Create a Directory, then expand Name.

checks.description: The new directory name was printed.

lessons.completion: New-Item works consistently across providers; the item type controls what is created.

lessons.title: Create a file with initial content
lessons.focus: -ItemType File and -Value create a usable file in one operation.
lessons.task: Create status.txt containing ready, then print its content.
lessons.solution: New-Item -ItemType File -Path status.txt -Value 'ready' | Out-Null; Get-Content status.txt
hints: Start with New-Item; use Get-Help New-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Create missing parent directories
lessons.focus: -Force allows New-Item to create a directory path whose parent segments do not yet exist.
lessons.task: Create the nested directory projectconfigproduction and print its leaf name.
hints: Start with New-Item; use Get-Help New-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Create several related directories
lessons.focus: -Path accepts an array so related items can be created and reviewed together.
lessons.task: Create bin, config, and logs directories in one New-Item call, then print their names sorted.
lessons.solution: New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path 'bin','config','logs' | Sort-Object Name | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name
hints: Start with New-Item; use Get-Help New-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Scaffold a small project
lessons.focus: Directory and file creation can be composed into an idempotent project scaffold.
lessons.example: New-Item project -ItemType Directory; New-Item projectREADME.md -ItemType File
lessons.task: Create appconfig and applogs, then create appconfigapp.ini containing mode=practice and print it.
lessons.solution: New-Item appconfig,applogs -ItemType Directory -Force | Out-Null; New-Item appconfigapp.ini -ItemType File -Value 'mode=practice' -Force | Out-Null; Get-Content appconfigapp.ini
hints: Start with New-Item; use Get-Help New-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Copy a file
lessons.focus: Copy-Item duplicates file-system items while leaving the source in place.
breakdown: The first path is the source.
The second path is the destination.
lessons.task: Copy source.txt to backup.txt without changing the source.
hints: Pass source and destination in that order.

checks.description: The backup contains the source text.

lessons.completion: Copy-Item is silent on success unless -PassThru is requested.

lessons.title: Overwrite a reviewed destination
lessons.focus: -Force replaces a read-only destination after the path has been deliberately selected.
lessons.task: Copy current.conf over the existing backup.conf with -Force, then print backup.conf.
hints: Start with Copy-Item; use Get-Help Copy-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Copy a directory recursively
lessons.focus: -Recurse copies a complete hierarchy rather than only its top-level item.
lessons.task: Copy project recursively to snapshot and print snapshotconfigapp.ini.
hints: Start with Copy-Item; use Get-Help Copy-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Copy a selected file set
lessons.focus: -Filter limits provider-side copying to matching names.
lessons.task: Copy only .json files from incoming into reviewed, then print copied names sorted.
lessons.solution: Copy-Item incoming* reviewed -Filter '*.json'; Get-ChildItem reviewed -File -Name | Sort-Object
hints: Start with Copy-Item; use Get-Help Copy-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Create a verified backup
lessons.focus: A practical copy workflow verifies content hashes instead of assuming the transfer succeeded.
lessons.example: Copy-Item artifact backup; Compare-Object (Get-FileHash artifact).Hash (Get-FileHash backup).Hash

hints: Start with Copy-Item; use Get-Help Copy-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Move a file
lessons.focus: Move-Item relocates an item and can give it a different destination name in one operation.
breakdown: The source is removed from its original path.
The destination may be a new relative path.
lessons.task: Move draft.txt to archive\final.txt.
hints: Use the complete destination path.

checks.description: The moved file has the original content.
The original draft path is gone.

lessons.completion: Move-Item changes location; Copy-Item deliberately keeps the source.

lessons.title: Move several files into a directory
lessons.focus: Move-Item accepts an array of reviewed source paths.

lessons.solution: Move-Item api.log,web.log archive; Get-ChildItem archive -File -Name | Sort-Object
hints: Start with Move-Item; use Get-Help Move-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Overwrite a stale destination
lessons.focus: -Force completes an intentional replacement when a destination file already exists.
lessons.task: Move new.conf over archiveapp.conf with -Force and print the result.
hints: Start with Move-Item; use Get-Help Move-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Move files selected by a pipeline
lessons.focus: Pipeline filtering lets metadata determine which paths are moved.

lessons.solution: Get-ChildItem queue -File | Where-Object Length -eq 0 | Move-Item -Destination empty; Get-ChildItem empty -File -Name | Sort-Object
hints: Start with Move-Item; use Get-Help Move-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Promote a staged release
lessons.focus: A move workflow can archive the old target and promote the reviewed staging tree atomically within one volume.

lessons.solution: Move-Item current archiveprevious; Move-Item staging current; Get-Content currentersion.txt
hints: Start with Move-Item; use Get-Help Move-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Rename an item
lessons.focus: Rename-Item changes an item's name while keeping it in the same parent location.
breakdown: The existing item comes first.
-NewName may also be used for clarity.
lessons.task: Rename report.draft to report.final.
hints: Provide the old and new names.

checks.description: The final report exists with its content.

lessons.completion: Rename-Item does not move an item to a different parent directory.

lessons.title: Rename with an explicit new name
lessons.focus: -NewName makes the destination leaf clear while keeping the item in its current directory.
lessons.task: Rename notes.old to notes.txt using -NewName.
hints: Start with Rename-Item; use Get-Help Rename-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Preview a rename
lessons.focus: -WhatIf shows the proposed rename without changing the file.
lessons.task: Preview renaming report.txt to report.bak without changing either path.
hints: Start with Rename-Item; use Get-Help Rename-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

hints: Start with Rename-Item; use Get-Help Rename-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Normalize numbered artifact names
lessons.focus: Pattern matching and formatted numbers can turn inconsistent names into a sortable convention.
lessons.task: Rename part-1.txt, part-2.txt, and part-10.txt to part-01.txt, part-02.txt, and part-10.txt, then print names sorted.
hints: Start with Rename-Item; use Get-Help Rename-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.focus: Remove-Item deletes provider items; this rep confines it to one synthetic file in the temporary workspace.

lessons.task: Delete the disposable file named trash.txt.
hints: Pass the file path directly.
lessons.completion: Use -WhatIf with Remove-Item outside a disposable workspace when reviewing a broad deletion.

lessons.title: Preview deletion safely
lessons.focus: -WhatIf reports the selected deletion without removing the item.
lessons.task: Preview deleting archive.log and keep the file intact.
hints: Start with Remove-Item; use Get-Help Remove-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Remove a directory recursively

lessons.task: Remove the disposable cache tree recursively while preserving data.
hints: Start with Remove-Item; use Get-Help Remove-Item -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Read file content
lessons.focus: Get-Content reads a text file as objects, usually emitting one string object per line.
breakdown: Each line enters the success pipeline separately.
-Raw can instead return one multiline string.

lessons.solution: $Run_Id=42; $Run_Status='done'; $Permanent='yes'; Get-Variable Run_* | Remove-Variable; "run-variables=$(@(Get-Variable Run_* -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Count) permanent=$Permanent"
hints: Start with Remove-Variable; use Get-Help Remove-Variable -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Inspect object properties and methods
lessons.focus: Get-Member reveals the type, properties, methods, events, and adapted members available on pipeline objects.
breakdown: The incoming FileInfo determines the member list.
-Name can narrow the inspection.
lessons.task: Confirm that note.txt's object exposes a member named Length.
lessons.solution: Get-Item note.txt | Get-Member -Name Length | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name
hints: Filter Get-Member with -Name Length.

checks.description: The Length member name was printed.

lessons.completion: Get-Member is the bridge from seeing output to understanding usable object data.

lessons.title: List methods only
lessons.focus: -MemberType Method narrows inspection to callable behavior.
lessons.task: Print the ToUpper method name from a string object.
hints: Start with Get-Member; use Get-Help Get-Member -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Inspect static members
lessons.focus: -Static exposes type-level members that do not require an instance.
lessons.task: Use Get-Member -Static on [datetime] and print the Today property name.
hints: Start with Get-Member; use Get-Help Get-Member -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Inspect an adapted object type

hints: Start with Get-Member; use Get-Help Get-Member -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Audit a command output schema

The host renders objects only at the pipeline's end.
lessons.task: Write alpha, beta, and gamma as three pipeline values.
hints: Pass the three values as arguments.

checks.description: All three values were emitted in order.

lessons.completion: Write-Output participates in the pipeline; Write-Host is presentation-oriented.

lessons.focus: -NoEnumerate keeps an array as one pipeline object.
lessons.task: Write the array 10,20,30 with -NoEnumerate and print count=3 after assigning the single output object.
hints: Start with Write-Output; use Get-Help Write-Output -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Use InputObject explicitly
lessons.focus: -InputObject makes the value being emitted clear in longer commands.
lessons.task: Emit status=ready using -InputObject.
hints: Start with Write-Output; use Get-Help Write-Output -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Feed output into a pipeline

Host output is intended for presentation.

hints: Start with Write-Host; use Get-Help Write-Host -Full if you need the parameter details.

hints: Start with Write-Host; use Get-Help Write-Host -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Format objects as a table

hints: Start with Format-Table; use Get-Help Format-Table -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Add a calculated table column
lessons.focus: Calculated properties derive display-only columns without mutating the source objects.
lessons.task: Format values.csv with name and a doubled column, then render it to text.
hints: Start with Format-Table; use Get-Help Format-Table -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Group table rows by a property
lessons.focus: -GroupBy adds headings when already-sorted objects change group value.

lessons.solution: Import-Csv hosts.csv | Sort-Object region,name | Format-Table name,status -GroupBy region | Out-String
hints: Start with Format-Table; use Get-Help Format-Table -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Create a compact status dashboard
lessons.focus: Selection, ordering, calculated display fields, and table formatting make an effective terminal dashboard.

hints: Start with Format-Table; use Get-Help Format-Table -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Format properties vertically

Each property appears on its own line.

hints: Format the two properties, then collect the display text.

checks.description: The list contains the name value.
The list contains the level value.

hints: Start with Format-List; use Get-Help Format-List -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Add a calculated list property
lessons.focus: Calculated properties can add derived values to a list view.
lessons.task: Format values.csv as name and doubled list fields, then render it.
hints: Start with Format-List; use Get-Help Format-List -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Format selected system details

hints: Start with Format-List; use Get-Help Format-List -Full if you need the parameter details.

hints: Start with Format-List; use Get-Help Format-List -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Convert display output to strings

-Stream avoids combining everything into one multiline string.

hints: Use the -Stream switch.

checks.description: The rendered note text was printed.

lessons.title: Render formatted output as one string
lessons.focus: Without -Stream, Out-String combines formatted output into one multiline scalar.
lessons.task: Format values.csv as a table, convert it to one string, and print string=True when the result is a string.
hints: Start with Out-String; use Get-Help Out-String -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Control rendering width
lessons.focus: -Width gives formatted objects enough horizontal space to avoid truncating important values.
lessons.task: Render records.csv as a table at width 200 and print the text containing the complete long value.
hints: Start with Out-String; use Get-Help Out-String -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Stream formatted lines for filtering
lessons.focus: -Stream emits individual rendered lines so normal text filtering can select from formatted output.
lessons.task: Format services.csv as a table, stream the rendered lines, and print only the line containing api.
lessons.solution: Import-Csv services.csv | Format-Table name,status | Out-String -Stream | Where-Object { $_ -match 'api' }
hints: Start with Out-String; use Get-Help Out-String -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Create a text report from objects
lessons.focus: Object formatting followed by Out-String creates a terminal-style report that can be labeled and saved.
lessons.task: Create report.txt beginning SERVICE REPORT and followed by an auto-sized name/status table from services.csv, then confirm api appears.
lessons.solution: $body=Import-Csv services.csv | Sort-Object name | Format-Table name,status -AutoSize | Out-String -Width 120; "SERVICE REPORT`n$body" | Set-Content report.txt; Get-Content report.txt -Raw
hints: Start with Out-String; use Get-Help Out-String -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Emit a warning stream message

hints: Pass the phrase as one quoted warning message.

checks.description: The warning did not fail the command.

lessons.completion: Warnings communicate concern without automatically terminating a script.

lessons.focus: -WarningVariable stores emitted warnings for later inspection while still displaying them.
lessons.task: Write warning disk space low into notice and print captured=disk space low.
hints: Start with Write-Warning; use Get-Help Write-Warning -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Suppress warning display
lessons.focus: -WarningAction SilentlyContinue hides presentation while WarningVariable can still retain the warning record.
lessons.task: Emit maintenance pending silently into warning variable w, then print stored=maintenance pending.
hints: Start with Write-Warning; use Get-Help Write-Warning -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Redirect warning output
lessons.focus: Stream 3 can be redirected into the success stream when a unified transcript is required.
lessons.task: Redirect the warning review configuration to success output and convert it to plain text.
hints: Start with Write-Warning; use Get-Help Write-Warning -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.focus: A workflow can preserve healthy data on the success stream while sending actionable concerns to the warning stream.

lessons.solution: $warnings=@(); Import-Csv services.csv | ForEach-Object { if($_.status -ne "up"){ Write-Warning "service $($_.name) is down" -WarningVariable +warnings } }; "warnings=$($warnings.Count)"
hints: Start with Write-Warning; use Get-Help Write-Warning -Full if you need the parameter details.

hints: Request the -Parent component.

hints: Start with Split-Path; use Get-Help Split-Path -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.task: Convert every .conf file and print their leaf names sorted.

hints: Start with Convert-Path; use Get-Help Convert-Path -Full if you need the parameter details.

Name Used (GB) Free (GB) Provider   Root
---- --------- --------- --------   ----
C                        FileSystem C:\

hints: Expand the Name property.

lessons.title: Create a provider capability matrix
lessons.focus: Provider metadata can be transformed into a compact namespace/capabilities audit.
lessons.task: Print Environment=<capabilities> and FileSystem=<capabilities> sorted by provider name.
hints: Start with Get-PSProvider; use Get-Help Get-PSProvider -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Read item properties

Select-Object can isolate one property value.
lessons.task: Print only the byte length property of note.txt.

ote.txt.

ote.txt

lessons.task: Randomize alpha, beta, and gamma with Get-Random -Count, then sort the result for verification and print all three.
hints: Start with Get-Random; use Get-Help Get-Random -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Create a bounded sample manifest
lessons.focus: Random sampling followed by validation can select a review subset while recording its constraints.
lessons.task: Select three distinct hosts from hosts.txt, save them to sample.txt, and print count=3 all-from-source=True.
hints: Start with Get-Random; use Get-Help Get-Random -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Inspect regional settings
lessons.focus: Get-Culture returns the current culture object used for formatting numbers, dates, currencies, and comparisons.
lessons.example_output:
LCID Name  DisplayName
---- ----  -----------
1033 en-US English (United States)
breakdown: Name is the culture identifier.
Other properties describe formatting conventions.
lessons.task: Print only the current culture name.
hints: Expand the Name property.

checks.description: The current culture name was printed.

lessons.completion: Culture affects parsing and formatting, so automation should make expectations explicit.

lessons.title: Read the date pattern
lessons.focus: DateTimeFormat exposes culture-specific patterns used by formatting and parsing.
lessons.task: Print a non-empty short-date pattern from the current culture.
hints: Start with Get-Culture; use Get-Help Get-Culture -Full if you need the parameter details.

checks.description: A short date pattern was printed.

lessons.title: Read numeric separators
lessons.focus: NumberFormat describes culture-specific decimal and grouping separators.
lessons.task: Print decimal=<value> group=<value> from the current culture.
hints: Start with Get-Culture; use Get-Help Get-Culture -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Round-trip a culture-formatted number
lessons.focus: Using the same culture for formatting and parsing avoids assumptions about decimal and group separators.
lessons.task: Format 1234.5 with the current culture, parse it with that culture, and print roundtrip=True.
hints: Start with Get-Culture; use Get-Help Get-Culture -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Create a culture diagnostics record
lessons.focus: A compact culture record makes parsing expectations explicit without assuming a particular locale.
lessons.task: Print name=<culture> decimal=<separator> date-pattern=<pattern> rtl=<True-or-False> from Get-Culture.
hints: Start with Get-Culture; use Get-Help Get-Culture -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Inspect the PowerShell host
lessons.focus: Get-Host returns information about the application hosting the PowerShell engine, including its version and capabilities.
breakdown: The host is separate from the operating system.
Version identifies the PowerShell host version.
lessons.task: Print the current host version as dotted text.
hints: Expand Version, then call its safe ToString member through ForEach-Object.

checks.description: A dotted PowerShell host version was printed.

lessons.completion: Host and engine versions help explain feature and behavior differences between environments.

lessons.title: Read the host name
lessons.focus: The Name property identifies the PowerShell host application running the session.
lessons.task: Print a non-empty PowerShell host name.
hints: Start with Get-Host; use Get-Help Get-Host -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Inspect host UI capabilities
lessons.focus: UI and RawUI objects expose interactive host dimensions and color settings when available.
lessons.task: Print width-positive=True for the current host window or buffer width.
hints: Start with Get-Host; use Get-Help Get-Host -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Read host culture settings
lessons.focus: CurrentCulture and CurrentUICulture show the formatting and resource cultures used by the host.
lessons.task: Print culture=<name> ui=<name> from Get-Host.
hints: Start with Get-Host; use Get-Help Get-Host -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Create a host diagnostic record
lessons.focus: A compact host record combines application identity, version, culture, and interactivity context.
lessons.task: Print name=<host> version=<version> culture=<culture> instance=<guid> from Get-Host.
hints: Start with Get-Host; use Get-Help Get-Host -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Query CIM system information
lessons.focus: Get-CimInstance queries Windows management data and returns structured CIM instances without screen scraping.
lessons.example_output:
SystemDirectory Organization BuildNumber RegisteredUser SerialNumber Version
...
breakdown: Win32_OperatingSystem names a CIM class.
The result exposes system properties as object members.
lessons.task: Print only the operating-system caption from CIM.
hints: Query the class, then expand Caption.

checks.description: A Windows operating-system caption was printed.

lessons.completion: CIM queries are a structured foundation for Windows inventory and diagnostics.

lessons.title: Query selected OS properties
lessons.focus: -Property requests only the CIM fields needed by the workflow.
lessons.task: Print caption=<value> version=<value> for Win32_OperatingSystem.
hints: Start with Get-CimInstance; use Get-Help Get-CimInstance -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Filter logical disks in CIM
lessons.focus: -Filter applies a WQL predicate at the CIM provider instead of retrieving every instance.
lessons.task: Print device IDs for fixed logical disks, sorted.
lessons.solution: Get-CimInstance Win32_LogicalDisk -Filter 'DriveType=3' | Sort-Object DeviceID | Select-Object -ExpandProperty DeviceID
hints: Start with Get-CimInstance; use Get-Help Get-CimInstance -Full if you need the parameter details.

checks.description: At least one fixed logical disk was printed.

lessons.title: Query a CIM class namespace explicitly
lessons.focus: -Namespace makes the management namespace clear when class names might overlap.
lessons.task: Query Win32_ComputerSystem in root/cimv2 and print manufacturer=<value> model=<value>.
hints: Start with Get-CimInstance; use Get-Help Get-CimInstance -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Create a CIM health snapshot
lessons.focus: Several focused CIM queries can produce a compact host snapshot without parsing command-line text.
lessons.task: Print os=<caption> memory-gb=<positive-number> processors=<positive-count> using CIM.
hints: Start with Get-CimInstance; use Get-Help Get-CimInstance -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Collect broad computer information
lessons.focus: Get-ComputerInfo aggregates operating-system, hardware, firmware, and configuration details into one large object.
breakdown: Get-ComputerInfo can be relatively expensive.
Select-Object narrows the broad object early.
lessons.task: Print only the Windows product name.
hints: Expand WindowsProductName from the result.

checks.description: A Windows product name was printed.

lessons.completion: Select only the properties you need from broad inventory commands.

lessons.title: Select one computer-info property
lessons.focus: -Property limits the expensive inventory to requested fields.
lessons.task: Print a non-empty OsArchitecture value.
hints: Start with Get-ComputerInfo; use Get-Help Get-ComputerInfo -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Select properties by wildcard
lessons.focus: A property wildcard discovers related inventory fields such as Windows version details.
lessons.task: Request WindowsProductName and WindowsVersion and print product=<value> version=<value>.
hints: Start with Get-ComputerInfo; use Get-Help Get-ComputerInfo -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Read hardware summary fields
lessons.focus: Computer information combines operating system and computer-system inventory in one object.
lessons.task: Print manufacturer=<value> model=<value> from computer information.
hints: Start with Get-ComputerInfo; use Get-Help Get-ComputerInfo -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Export a focused support snapshot
lessons.focus: A selected computer-info object can be serialized as a small support artifact instead of dumping every property.
lessons.task: Write support.json with WindowsProductName, WindowsVersion, and OsArchitecture, then parse it and print fields=3.
lessons.solution: Get-ComputerInfo -Property WindowsProductName,WindowsVersion,OsArchitecture | Select-Object WindowsProductName,WindowsVersion,OsArchitecture | ConvertTo-Json | Set-Content support.json; $o=Get-Content support.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json; "fields=$(@($o.PSObject.Properties).Count)"
hints: Start with Get-ComputerInfo; use Get-Help Get-ComputerInfo -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: List installed Windows updates
lessons.focus: Get-HotFix reads installed update records and returns identifiers, descriptions, installation dates, and related metadata.
breakdown: The command is read-only.
The first record is sufficient for a short inventory rep.
lessons.task: Print the HotFixID of the first installed update record.
hints: Select the first record and expand HotFixID.

checks.description: A Windows update identifier was printed.

lessons.completion: Update inventory is one signal; support status and deployment policy require additional context.

lessons.title: Count installed hotfix records
lessons.focus: Wrapping output in an array gives a reliable count even when a machine reports zero or one record.
lessons.task: Print hotfix-count=<nonnegative-count>.
hints: Start with Get-HotFix; use Get-Help Get-HotFix -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Select common hotfix fields
lessons.focus: HotFixID, Description, and InstalledOn form a useful update inventory projection.
lessons.task: Print id:description records for up to the first three hotfixes; print none if no records exist.
hints: Start with Get-HotFix; use Get-Help Get-HotFix -Full if you need the parameter details.

checks.description: A hotfix inventory result was printed.

lessons.title: Sort update records by installation date
lessons.focus: Sorting InstalledOn descending surfaces the newest recorded updates first.
lessons.task: Print newest=<HotFixID> for the newest dated hotfix, or newest=none when no records exist.
hints: Start with Get-HotFix; use Get-Help Get-HotFix -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Create a hotfix summary by description
lessons.focus: Grouping hotfix objects by Description produces a concise update-category summary.
lessons.task: Print description=count rows sorted, or no-hotfix-records if none are returned.
lessons.solution: $h=@(Get-HotFix); if($h.Count){$h | Group-Object Description | Sort-Object Name | ForEach-Object { "$($_.Name)=$($_.Count)" }}else{"no-hotfix-records"}
hints: Start with Get-HotFix; use Get-Help Get-HotFix -Full if you need the parameter details.

checks.description: A grouped hotfix summary was printed.

lessons.title: Inspect physical disks
lessons.focus: Get-Disk returns Windows disk objects with numbers, sizes, partition styles, health, and operational status.
lessons.example_output:
Number Friendly Name Serial Number HealthStatus OperationalStatus Total Size Partition Style
------ ------------- ------------- ------------ ----------------- ---------- ---------------
0      ...                         Healthy      Online            ...        GPT
breakdown: Disk numbers identify storage devices in management cmdlets.
This rep performs read-only inspection.
lessons.task: Print the number of the first disk Windows reports.
hints: Select the first disk and expand Number.

checks.description: A numeric disk identifier was printed.

lessons.completion: Disk operations can be destructive; begin with read-only inventory and verify identifiers carefully.

lessons.title: Read disk health status
lessons.focus: HealthStatus provides a quick management-layer assessment for each disk.
lessons.task: Print disk=<number> health=<status> for the first disk.
hints: Start with Get-Disk; use Get-Help Get-Disk -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Report disk sizes
lessons.focus: Disk Size is a byte count that can be converted to readable gigabytes.
lessons.task: Print disk=<number> size-gb=<positive-value> for every disk.
hints: Start with Get-Disk; use Get-Help Get-Disk -Full if you need the parameter details.

checks.description: A disk size report was printed.

lessons.title: Filter disks by operational status
lessons.focus: Filtering BusType or OperationalStatus focuses the inventory on disks relevant to a workflow.
lessons.task: Print online-disks=<count> for disks whose OperationalStatus contains Online.
hints: Start with Get-Disk; use Get-Help Get-Disk -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Create a disk inventory record
lessons.focus: Selected disk identity, bus, partition style, size, and health provide a practical storage snapshot.
lessons.task: Print number|bus|partition|size-gb|health for each disk sorted by number.
hints: Start with Get-Disk; use Get-Help Get-Disk -Full if you need the parameter details.

checks.description: A detailed disk inventory was printed.

lessons.title: Inspect mounted volumes
lessons.focus: Get-Volume returns volume objects with drive letters, labels, file systems, sizes, and health state.
lessons.example_output:
DriveLetter FriendlyName FileSystemType DriveType HealthStatus SizeRemaining Size
----------- ------------ -------------- --------- ------------ ------------- ----
C                        NTFS           Fixed     Healthy      ...           ...
breakdown: Volumes are distinct from physical disks.
DriveLetter can be null for unlettered volumes.
lessons.task: Print the first non-empty drive letter.
hints: Filter out null DriveLetter values before selecting the first.
lessons.completion: Volumes expose file systems and capacity; disks represent underlying storage devices.

lessons.title: Read volume file-system details
lessons.focus: Volume objects expose drive letter, filesystem type, and health.
lessons.task: Print drive=<letter> filesystem=<type> for the first drive-letter volume.
lessons.solution: $v=Get-Volume | Where-Object DriveLetter | Sort-Object DriveLetter | Select-Object -First 1; "drive=$($v.DriveLetter) filesystem=$($v.FileSystem)"
hints: Start with Get-Volume; use Get-Help Get-Volume -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Report free space
lessons.focus: SizeRemaining and Size can be converted into readable capacity metrics.
lessons.task: Print drive=<letter> free-gb=<nonnegative> for each drive-letter volume.
lessons.solution: Get-Volume | Where-Object DriveLetter | Sort-Object DriveLetter | ForEach-Object { "drive=$($_.DriveLetter) free-gb=$([math]::Round($_.SizeRemaining/1GB,1))" }
hints: Start with Get-Volume; use Get-Help Get-Volume -Full if you need the parameter details.

checks.description: A volume free-space report was printed.

lessons.title: Find volumes needing attention
lessons.focus: HealthStatus filtering identifies volumes whose management status is not Healthy.
lessons.task: Print unhealthy-volumes=<count>.
hints: Start with Get-Volume; use Get-Help Get-Volume -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Create a volume capacity summary
lessons.focus: A practical volume report calculates used percentage from size and remaining space without changing storage.
lessons.task: Print drive=<letter> used-percent=<number> health=<status> for each drive-letter volume.
lessons.solution: Get-Volume | Where-Object { $_.DriveLetter -and $_.Size -gt 0 } | Sort-Object DriveLetter | ForEach-Object { $used=100*(1-$_.SizeRemaining/$_.Size); "drive=$($_.DriveLetter) used-percent=$([math]::Round($used,1)) health=$($_.HealthStatus)" }
hints: Start with Get-Volume; use Get-Help Get-Volume -Full if you need the parameter details.

checks.description: A volume capacity summary was printed.

lessons.title: Inspect assigned IP addresses
lessons.focus: Get-NetIPAddress returns structured address assignments across Windows network interfaces.
lessons.example_output:
IPAddress InterfaceIndex InterfaceAlias AddressFamily Type PrefixLength PrefixOrigin SuffixOrigin AddressState PolicyStore
...
breakdown: -AddressFamily narrows the query to IPv4.
Each result includes address and interface properties.
lessons.task: Print the first IPv4 address Windows reports.
hints: Filter by IPv4 and expand IPAddress.
lessons.completion: Address objects retain interface, prefix, origin, and state information for later filtering.

lessons.title: Filter by address family
lessons.focus: -AddressFamily limits results to IPv4 or IPv6 before pipeline processing.
lessons.task: Print ipv4-count=<positive-count> for IPv4 addresses.
hints: Start with Get-NetIPAddress; use Get-Help Get-NetIPAddress -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Select addresses for one interface
lessons.focus: -InterfaceAlias targets a named adapter instead of filtering a full address table afterward.
lessons.task: Find the first IPv4 interface alias, query that alias explicitly, and print alias=<name> addresses=<count>.
hints: Start with Get-NetIPAddress; use Get-Help Get-NetIPAddress -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Inspect prefix metadata
lessons.focus: PrefixLength and AddressState provide subnet and lifecycle context for each IP address.
lessons.task: Print address/prefix state=<state> rows for IPv4 addresses, sorted by address.
lessons.solution: Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Sort-Object IPAddress | ForEach-Object { "$($_.IPAddress)/$($_.PrefixLength) state=$($_.AddressState)" }
hints: Start with Get-NetIPAddress; use Get-Help Get-NetIPAddress -Full if you need the parameter details.

checks.description: An IPv4 prefix report was printed.

lessons.title: Create a usable-address inventory
lessons.focus: Filtering address state and origin fields creates a concise interface/address inventory for diagnostics.
lessons.task: Print alias=address/prefix for preferred IPv4 addresses, sorted by alias then address.
lessons.solution: Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Where-Object AddressState -eq Preferred | Sort-Object InterfaceAlias,IPAddress | ForEach-Object { "$($_.InterfaceAlias)=$($_.IPAddress)/$($_.PrefixLength)" }
hints: Start with Get-NetIPAddress; use Get-Help Get-NetIPAddress -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Summarize interface configuration
lessons.focus: Get-NetIPConfiguration summarizes adapters, IP addresses, gateways, and DNS servers as related objects.
lessons.example_output:
InterfaceAlias : Ethernet
InterfaceIndex : 4
IPv4Address    : 10.0.0.5
IPv4DefaultGateway : ...
DNSServer : ...
breakdown: Each object represents one interface configuration.
InterfaceAlias is a human-readable adapter name.
lessons.task: Print the alias of the first configured network interface.
hints: Select the first object and expand InterfaceAlias.

checks.description: A network interface alias was printed.

lessons.completion: Use the related address, gateway, and DNS properties instead of parsing ipconfig text.

lessons.title: Inspect detailed configuration
lessons.focus: -Detailed includes additional adapter, route, DNS, and profile information.
lessons.task: Print detailed-count=<positive-count> for network configurations.
hints: Start with Get-NetIPConfiguration; use Get-Help Get-NetIPConfiguration -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Query one interface alias
lessons.focus: -InterfaceAlias requests one configuration directly.
lessons.task: Find the first interface alias, query it with -InterfaceAlias, and print its alias.
hints: Start with Get-NetIPConfiguration; use Get-Help Get-NetIPConfiguration -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Read IPv4 and gateway context
lessons.focus: Nested IPv4Address and IPv4DefaultGateway properties describe host and route configuration together.
lessons.task: Print alias=<name> ipv4=<value-or-none> gateway=<value-or-none> for the first configuration.
hints: Start with Get-NetIPConfiguration; use Get-Help Get-NetIPConfiguration -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Create an interface configuration summary
lessons.focus: Flattening nested configuration properties creates a practical one-line record per interface.
lessons.task: Print alias|ipv4-count|dns-count records for every interface, sorted by alias.
hints: Start with Get-NetIPConfiguration; use Get-Help Get-NetIPConfiguration -Full if you need the parameter details.

checks.description: An interface configuration summary was printed.

lessons.title: Inspect network adapters
lessons.focus: Get-NetAdapter returns physical and virtual network adapter objects with status, speed, names, and interface details.
lessons.example_output:
Name InterfaceDescription ifIndex Status MacAddress LinkSpeed
---- -------------------- ------- ------ ---------- ---------
Ethernet ...              4       Up     ...        10 Gbps
breakdown: Status identifies whether the adapter is operational.
Name is suitable for later adapter cmdlets.
lessons.task: Print the name of the first network adapter.
hints: Select the first adapter and expand Name.

checks.description: A network adapter name was printed.

lessons.completion: Adapter inventory is read-only here; changing adapters can disconnect a machine.

lessons.title: Read adapter status
lessons.focus: Status reports whether a network adapter is operationally Up or disconnected.
lessons.task: Print name=status for the first network adapter.
hints: Start with Get-NetAdapter; use Get-Help Get-NetAdapter -Full if you need the parameter details.

checks.description: An adapter status record was printed.

lessons.title: Include hidden adapters
lessons.focus: -IncludeHidden includes adapters omitted from the default view.
lessons.task: Print visible=<count> all=<count> and verify all is not smaller than visible.
hints: Start with Get-NetAdapter; use Get-Help Get-NetAdapter -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Inspect link properties
lessons.focus: LinkSpeed, MacAddress, and InterfaceDescription provide physical and virtual adapter context.
lessons.task: Print name|status|link-speed records for all adapters sorted by name.
hints: Start with Get-NetAdapter; use Get-Help Get-NetAdapter -Full if you need the parameter details.

checks.description: An adapter link report was printed.

lessons.title: Create an active-adapter inventory
lessons.focus: Filtering Up adapters and selecting stable fields yields a concise connectivity snapshot.
lessons.task: Print up-adapters=<count>, then name=mac records for every Up adapter sorted by name.
lessons.solution: $up=@(Get-NetAdapter | Where-Object Status -eq Up | Sort-Object Name); "up-adapters=$($up.Count)"; $up | ForEach-Object { "$($_.Name)=$($_.MacAddress)" }
hints: Start with Get-NetAdapter; use Get-Help Get-NetAdapter -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Inspect the routing table
lessons.focus: Get-NetRoute returns Windows routing entries as objects with destinations, next hops, metrics, and interfaces.
lessons.example_output:
ifIndex DestinationPrefix NextHop RouteMetric ifMetric PolicyStore
------- ----------------- ------- ----------- -------- -----------
...
breakdown: -AddressFamily narrows the route set.
DestinationPrefix represents a routed network.
lessons.task: Print the first IPv4 destination prefix.
hints: Expand DestinationPrefix from the first IPv4 route.

checks.description: An IPv4 destination prefix was printed.

lessons.completion: Route objects can be filtered by interface, destination, and metric without parsing columns.

lessons.title: Find default IPv4 routes
lessons.focus: DestinationPrefix 0.0.0.0/0 identifies IPv4 default-route candidates.
lessons.task: Print default-routes=<count> for IPv4 default routes.
hints: Start with Get-NetRoute; use Get-Help Get-NetRoute -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Inspect route metrics
lessons.focus: RouteMetric and InterfaceMetric help explain which candidate route Windows prefers.
lessons.task: Print prefix metric=<route-metric> interface=<index> for the first IPv4 route.
lessons.solution: $r=Get-NetRoute -AddressFamily IPv4 | Sort-Object RouteMetric | Select-Object -First 1; "$($r.DestinationPrefix) metric=$($r.RouteMetric) interface=$($r.InterfaceIndex)"
hints: Start with Get-NetRoute; use Get-Help Get-NetRoute -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Filter routes by interface
lessons.focus: -InterfaceIndex targets the route table associated with one selected adapter.
lessons.task: Find the first IPv4 route interface index, query it explicitly, and print route-count=<count>.
hints: Start with Get-NetRoute; use Get-Help Get-NetRoute -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Create a route decision report
lessons.focus: Sorting by combined route and interface metrics provides a useful view of candidate preference.
lessons.task: Print the five lowest-metric IPv4 routes as prefix via next-hop metric=total.
lessons.solution: Get-NetRoute -AddressFamily IPv4 | Sort-Object @{Expression={$_.RouteMetric+$_.InterfaceMetric}} | Select-Object -First 5 | ForEach-Object { "$($_.DestinationPrefix) via $($_.NextHop) metric=$($_.RouteMetric+$_.InterfaceMetric)" }
hints: Start with Get-NetRoute; use Get-Help Get-NetRoute -Full if you need the parameter details.

checks.description: A ranked route report was printed.

lessons.title: Inspect TCP endpoints
lessons.focus: Get-NetTCPConnection returns local TCP listeners and connections with addresses, ports, state, and owning process identifiers.
lessons.example_output:
LocalAddress LocalPort RemoteAddress RemotePort State OwningProcess
------------ --------- ------------- ---------- ----- -------------
0.0.0.0      135       0.0.0.0       0          Listen ...
breakdown: -State Listen narrows the collection.
OwningProcess can be correlated with Get-Process.
lessons.task: Print the state of the first listening TCP endpoint.
hints: Query listening endpoints and expand State.
lessons.completion: Connection objects preserve ports, addresses, states, and owning process IDs for correlation.

lessons.title: Count listening endpoints
lessons.focus: -State Listen limits results to local TCP listeners.
lessons.task: Print listeners=<count>.
hints: Start with Get-NetTCPConnection; use Get-Help Get-NetTCPConnection -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Inspect local listening ports
lessons.focus: LocalAddress and LocalPort identify where each listener accepts connections.
lessons.task: Print unique listening local ports in numeric order.
hints: Start with Get-NetTCPConnection; use Get-Help Get-NetTCPConnection -Full if you need the parameter details.

checks.description: At least one listening port was printed.

lessons.title: Associate connections with processes
lessons.focus: OwningProcess links TCP endpoints to process records.
lessons.task: Print port=process for up to five listening TCP endpoints with resolvable owning processes.
lessons.solution: Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen | Sort-Object LocalPort | Select-Object -First 5 | ForEach-Object { $p=Get-Process -Id $_.OwningProcess -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if($p){"$($_.LocalPort)=$($p.ProcessName)"} }
hints: Start with Get-NetTCPConnection; use Get-Help Get-NetTCPConnection -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Create a TCP state summary
lessons.focus: Grouping TCP connection objects by State creates a compact socket inventory.
lessons.task: Print state=count rows for all TCP connections sorted by state.
lessons.solution: Get-NetTCPConnection | Group-Object State | Sort-Object Name | ForEach-Object { "$($_.Name)=$($_.Count)" }
hints: Start with Get-NetTCPConnection; use Get-Help Get-NetTCPConnection -Full if you need the parameter details.

checks.description: A TCP state summary was printed.

lessons.title: Test loopback reachability
lessons.focus: Test-Connection sends ICMP echo requests and returns response objects; this rep is restricted to the local loopback name.
lessons.example_output:
Source Destination IPV4Address IPV6Address Bytes Time(ms)
------ ----------- ----------- ----------- ----- --------
...    localhost   127.0.0.1               32    0
breakdown: localhost keeps traffic on this machine.
-Count 1 performs one short probe.
lessons.task: Send one loopback probe and print its Address property.
hints: Use localhost and -Count 1, then expand Address.

checks.description: The loopback response address was printed.

lessons.completion: A successful echo confirms only this narrow path, not application availability.

lessons.title: Return a Boolean connectivity result
lessons.focus: -Quiet returns True or False instead of probe objects.
lessons.task: Test localhost once in quiet mode and print reachable=True.
hints: Start with Test-Connection; use Get-Help Test-Connection -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Test the IPv4 loopback address
lessons.focus: Using 127.0.0.1 tests the IPv4 loopback path without depending on name resolution.
lessons.task: Send one IPv4 loopback probe and print ipv4=True when it succeeds.
hints: Start with Test-Connection; use Get-Help Test-Connection -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Inspect response-time data
lessons.focus: Windows PowerShell probe objects expose ResponseTime and address details for diagnostics.
lessons.task: Send two localhost probes and print replies=2 nonnegative-latency=True.
hints: Start with Test-Connection; use Get-Help Test-Connection -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Build a target reachability report
lessons.focus: Quiet probes across a reviewed target list produce a concise Boolean preflight report.
lessons.task: Read targets.txt and print localhost=True and 127.0.0.1=True.
hints: Start with Test-Connection; use Get-Help Test-Connection -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Resolve the local host name
lessons.focus: Resolve-DnsName performs structured DNS queries; this offline rep is limited to the local host name.
lessons.example_output:
Name Type TTL Section IPAddress
---- ---- --- ------- ---------
localhost A   ... Answer 127.0.0.1
breakdown: localhost avoids an external DNS dependency.
Returned records expose names, types, and addresses.
lessons.task: Resolve localhost and print the first record's Name property.
hints: Resolve only localhost, then expand Name.

checks.description: The local host name was resolved.

lessons.completion: Structured DNS records are easier to filter by record type than nslookup display text.

lessons.title: Request an A record
lessons.focus: -Type A limits resolution to IPv4 address records.
lessons.task: Resolve localhost as type A and print at least one IPv4 address.
hints: Start with Resolve-DnsName; use Get-Help Resolve-DnsName -Full if you need the parameter details.

lessons.title: Use DNS-only mode with fallback
